round3.root_cause: Round 2 pinned the bundle at priority 1, below every installed package, so apt could never upgrade an installed package from the bundle. An air-gapped host lags on patches, so any new package whose dependency needs a newer build of an installed library cannot resolve. The pin conflated 'never replace a FIPS package' with 'never upgrade anything'.

root_cause.N1: requirements.lock had three readers with three rule sets. Round 10 moved the gate to pip's rules but gen-requirements-lock.py lock_set() (--check-set) and sca-check.sh kept raw column-0 regexes. A comment ending in a backslash makes pip join the next entry into the comment: pip and the gate lose it while the column-0 readers still count it (X20: cffi gone, --check-set 'covers', gate PASS 14 releases). An indented entry is read by pip but not by a column-0 regex (X21: pip installs pyasn1 0.4.8, --check-set and SCA see the swallowed 0.6.4). The round-10 claim that lock_set() was 'not affected' was false: it was the second parser.
root_cause.TM-RL-004: the gate split requirement lines on any whitespace (\s+); pip splits on the space character only, so a TAB before --hash is one malformed requirement to pip.
root_cause.TM-RL-005: the gate accepted --check-set's exit 0 without reading its verdict or count; resolve() had no timeout.
root_cause.TM-RL-002: sca skipped any line its regex did not match (indented entries) and its only floor was '> 0 transitive pins'; it also skipped a lock entry whenever requirements.txt had the same NAME, so it queried requirements.txt's version rather than the one pip installs.
